why: Each group adds +passengers at 'from' and -passengers at 'to'; the seats needed is the peak of the running sum of these events in position order. Coordinates up to 10^9 rule out a difference array, so sort the events (a sweep line, i.e. prefix sums over sorted points).
hints: Only the points where people get in or out matter; occupancy is constant between them.
Turn each trip into two events (from, +p) and (to, -p). At equal positions, drop-offs must be processed before pick-ups.
Sort events by (position, delta) so negative deltas come first at ties, sweep with a running sum, and track the maximum. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Tie order: at a shared point, leaving before entering (example 2 answers 3, not 5). Sorting tuples (pos, delta) handles it because negative deltas sort first.
Positions reach 10^9, so do not allocate an array indexed by position.
The answer is the peak occupancy, not the total number of passengers.
